name: Two Section Overlaps Control Rooted Transfer without Containment
statement: Use the canonical degree-two-corner presentation $Y=\{(0,00)\}\cup(A\times\{01\})\cup(D\times\{10\})\cup(C\times\{11\})$ and its four shadow conditions. Put $R=A\cap C$ and $S=D\cap C$. Suppose $R,S$ are dismantlable ample and that $A$ and $C$ peel relatively to $R$, while $D$ and $C$ peel relatively to $S$. Then $Y$ is dismantlable ample and peels to $a=(0,00)$ exactly when either $R$ and $D$ both peel to zero or $S$ and $A$ both peel to zero. Every endpoint in another section is attainable in $Y$ exactly when it is attainable in that section. If every old coordinate is active in $A\cup D\cup C$, then $(Y,a)$ is a rooted factor exactly when $A,D$ peel to zero, neither $R$ nor $S$ peels to zero, and every root-preserving elementary old-coordinate image makes at least one of the image overlaps root-positive. The root $a$ is then the unique critical root. If $(R,0)$ and $(S,0)$ are rooted factors using all old coordinates, the last condition is automatic; no containment of $C$ in either side is required.
proof: The four shadow conditions give ampleness. Isometry rules out words in $(A\cap D)\setminus C$ and edges between the exclusive parts of adjacent sections, so the assumed relative orders remain valid in the unions. Clearing the appropriate exclusive pieces gives relative orders to each section and proves ordinary positivity and every nonroot endpoint formula. For a root-ending order, the first deleted nonroot copy of zero and a broken-fiber projection force either $R$ or $S$ to peel to zero, while explicit section-clearing orders prove both converse alternatives. Relative orders and intersections commute with root-preserving coordinate images. Applying the endpoint equivalence to each image yields the three rooted-minimality conditions; explicit orders handle the two new-coordinate restrictions and contractions. Any other unattainable vertex already fails in its proper section, proving uniqueness of the critical root.
